2609.02143.title: A Power Law in Logarithm's Clothing: On the Scalability of Graph-Based Vector Search
2609.02143.paper_summary: Most vector databases rely on graph-based indexes, notably HNSW and Vamana, for approximate nearest neighbor search. With embedding models widely adopted, the datasets these databases store grow rapidly. At a fixed accuracy, how does search cost scale with dataset size? The prevailing answer is poly-logarithmic growth. Yet the claim is proven only under special conditions and asserted without proof for the indexes used in practice. It is also largely untested: standard benchmarks measure cost at one dataset size, not across sizes. We put the claim to the test. The answer depends on the scale itself. While the dataset size $N$ is small relative to the data's intrinsic dimensionality, search cost grows as $N^c$ for a constant $0<c<1$. We call this scaling the Sublinear Power Law. Once $N$ is large enough, growth slows to subpolynomial, consistent with the poly-logarithmic claim. The Sublinear Power Law appears on every dataset, mostly up to its full size, at every recall target, query hardness level, and index configuration we test. The transition to subpolynomial growth appears on the two datasets that grow large enough relative to their intrinsic dimensionality. One mechanism underlies both behaviors: a dataset's intrinsic dimensionality grows with its size until the data resolves its underlying distribution. Higher intrinsic dimensionality packs more vectors into the query neighborhood the search must examine. We present a unifying theory of beam-search cost that explains our observations. For exact and bounded-degree constructions, we prove the Sublinear Power Law and the eventual transition to poly-logarithmic scaling, and derive the scale at which it occurs. We also develop models that predict the power-law exponents for any recall target and index configuration. These models give a principled way to navigate trade-offs among search cost, insertion cost, and recall as data grows.
2609.02143.paper_summary_zh: 大多數向量資料庫依賴於基於圖形的索引，特別是 HNSW 和 Vamana，用於近似最近鄰搜索。隨著嵌入模型的廣泛採用，這些資料庫儲存的數據集迅速增長。在固定的準確度下，搜索成本如何隨著數據集大小的增長而變化？普遍的答案是多對數增長。然而，這一說法僅在特殊條件下得到證明，且對實際使用的索引未提供證明。這一說法也在很大程度上未經測試：標準基準測試在一個數據集大小下測量成本，而不是跨越不同大小。我們對這一說法進行了測試。答案取決於規模本身。當數據集大小 $N$ 相對於數據的內在維度較小時，搜索成本隨著 $N^c$ 增長，其中常數滿足 $0<c<1$。我們稱這種增長為次線性冪律。一旦 $N$ 足夠大，增長速度會減緩至次多項式，這與多對數的說法一致。次線性冪律在每個數據集上都出現，主要是在其完整大小之前，並且在我們測試的每個召回目標、查詢難度級別和索引配置下均如此。轉變為次多項式增長出現在兩個相對於其內在維度增長足夠大的數據集上。這兩種行為背後有一個共同的機制：數據集的內在維度隨著其大小增長，直到數據解析其潛在分佈。更高的內在維度將更多的向量包裝進查詢鄰域中，搜索必須檢查這些向量。我們提出了一個統一的束搜索成本理論，解釋了我們的觀察結果。對於精確和有界度的構造，我們證明了次線性冪律及最終轉變為多對數增長，並推導出其發生的規模。我們還開發了模型，預測任何召回目標和索引配置的冪律指數。這些模型提供了一種原則性的方法，以在數據增長過程中導航搜索成本、插入成本和召回之間的權衡。
